changelog:
**Creating a channel made the whole plugin unsaveable, and that is fixed.** The page built every new channel with a trailer mode the server has never had a name for. A plugin's configuration is saved as **one document**, so the one unreadable value failed the whole of it: the server answered 500 and *nothing* could be saved - not the new channel, and not the channels that were already there and perfectly valid. Saving is guarded by a test now that reads the page's own source and checks every value it writes against the enum the server reads it into.

**A new channel no longer opens on an error.** It exists only in the page until you press Save, and every schedule endpoint answers "no such channel" until then - which was printed raw over an empty week. The page asks first, says the channel has not been saved yet, and the week appears by itself the moment Save lands.

**Every failure on the page used to read `[object Response]`.** Jellyfin hands back the response rather than an error, so nothing could report what actually went wrong - not the code, not the route. Failures say both now, which is how the save fault above was found.

**Pictures can be cropped.** Press Crop on any of a channel's three pictures and set exactly which part of it the television uses: drag to move, scroll to zoom, and zoom out past the edges when an upright picture has to go in a five-to-one banner - the space that opens is filled with a blurred copy of the picture rather than a black bar.

**The picture search works, and looks like it.** Clicking a picture used to do nothing at all unless a slot had been armed first; now a click offers the three slots. The filters are named after what they fill - Banner, Poster, Backdrop - rather than by shape, and the online search asks the providers for the thing itself: **TheTVDB has real banners for a series**, which the page could never have been offered before because it asked for a thumbnail. Your own library is asked the same question. The wall is a plain grid in the shape of the slot, so the rows are even and flush instead of ragged, and it fetches a screenful at a time with a button for more.

**The three preview pictures are the shapes they really are** - the banner across its own row, the backdrop and poster beneath - instead of three boxes of one size, in which a five-to-one banner could not be judged at all.

The rest: searches no longer show titles that do not match (a slow answer to an earlier keystroke could land last and overwrite the right one); "Not that - show me another" says when there is no other lineup rather than silently offering the same one; a picture put on the shelf while a series is open is visible instead of landing behind it; and "1 seasons" counts properly.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
